words.gram: Noun in the idiom 気が向く (feel like doing).

lines.trans: Forget the past and it is easy money. Quite a luxury of a dilemma, right?
Having something more precious than money actually makes me envious.
I will find another way to earn, so please spare me the adult-video world.
I value this guy highly. Let him walk you home tonight.
Say, what do yakuza actually do during the daytime?
Well, all sorts of things.
If you hate it, why don't you just quit?
Don't talk like it is a part-time job. You can't quit that easily.

words.gram: Auxiliary na-adjective expressing appearance or likeness.
Plain dictionary form of 言う (to say).

lines.trans: Still, this life doesn't suit you, Toshi. Cheer up.
Thanks for walking me home. Good night.

words.gram: Plain imperative of くれる (give/do for me).

lines.trans: It is on my way back anyway, so I will walk you home again.

meanings.note: Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).
All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.

examples.text: 監督、時間です。急ぎましょう。
examples.trans: Director, it is time to go. Let's hurry.

examples.text: いらねえよ！嫌いなんだようなぎはよ。
examples.trans: I don't want it! I hate eel anyway.

meanings.en: do for an inferior (tough-guy てやる)
meanings.note: After て-form (勘弁してやる), expresses granting a favor from a position of authority.

examples.trans: I will give you a hand (casual masculine).

meanings.note: Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.

examples.text: 過去さえ忘れりゃ簡単にもうけられる仕事だ。贅沢な悩みだろ？
examples.trans: Forget the past and it is easy money. Quite a luxury of a dilemma, right?

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Na-adjective; 簡単に means 'easily'.

examples.text: そう簡単に売れないよ。

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.
Everyday noun for one's job or workplace duties.

examples.text: 新しい仕事は楽しいです。
これから仕事に行きます。
examples.trans: I am heading to work now.

meanings.note: Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.

examples.text: 過去さえ忘れりゃ簡単にもうけられる仕事だ。贅沢な悩みだろ？
examples.trans: Forget the past and it is easy money. Quite a luxury of a dilemma, right?

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: casual reflection or firm reminder particle
meanings.note: Used aloud to oneself ('man, I'm hungry') or at the end of a warning ('remember that, okay?').

examples.text: 過去さえ忘れりゃ簡単にもうけられる仕事だ。贅沢な悩みだろ？
examples.trans: Forget the past and it is easy money. Quite a luxury of a dilemma, right?

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: whichever (after question word); or something like
meanings.note: After どれ (どれでも) means 'any one at all'; after a noun (店でも) suggests an example ('a shop or something').

examples.text: いつでも来てください。
お茶でも飲みませんか。
examples.trans: Won't you have tea or something?

meanings.note: Polite/standard form of 金 (かね) with honorific prefix お.
Replaces は, が, or を to add 'also' or 'too'.

examples.trans: Please give me this one too.

examples.text: あそこも新しい店です。
examples.trans: Over there is a new shop too.

meanings.note: Read なん before だ/です/の, and なに before が/を or alone.

examples.text: 何を買いにきましたか。
examples.trans: What did you come to buy?

meanings.note: Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

meanings.en: exist; be available; remain in place
meanings.note: Used for inanimate things and abstract concepts; after て-form (書いてある, 置いてある) describes a resulting state left in place.

examples.text: 名前が書いてあります。

meanings.note: Colloquial quotative/emphatic particle expressing surprise or dismissal.

examples.text: そんなことなんて知らない。
examples.trans: I don't know anything like that.

examples.text: 嘘だなんて信じられない。
examples.trans: I can't believe it's a lie.

examples.text: でもお金よりも大切な何かがあるなんて、羨ましいですよ。
examples.trans: Having something more precious than money actually makes me envious.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Polite sentence-ending counterpart of plain だ.

cells: ではありません / じゃありません

meanings.note: Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.
Used for the physical world or a specific sphere/industry (この世界).

examples.text: この世界に入る覚悟はあるか。
examples.trans: Are you prepared to enter this world?

meanings.note: Limits the preceding noun or phrase to that item alone.

examples.text: これだけお願いします。

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.
Follows a verb's て-form or polite お + stem (お待ちください, お持ち帰りください) to make a polite request.

examples.text: ここに書いてください。

meanings.note: Used among friends and peers by men; switch to 私 or 僕 in formal settings.
Refers to facts, matters, or affairs rather than physical objects (もの).

examples.text: 仕事のことを話します。

meanings.note: 買えます is the polite potential form meaning 'can buy / can afford to buy'.

examples.text: 本屋で雑誌を買いました。
examples.trans: I bought a magazine at the bookstore.

examples.text: この値段なら買えますよ。
examples.trans: At this price, we can buy it.

examples.text: お前ら、観光じゃないんだからしっかりしろよ。
examples.trans: Hey, this isn't sightseeing, so pull yourselves together.

examples.text: 彼女は来るんだろうな？
ちゃんとキャストはそろってるんだろうな？
examples.trans: You've got the whole cast properly lined up, right?

meanings.note: Can stand at the head of a sentence without a particle ('right now').

examples.text: ねえ、ヤクザってさ、昼間何してんの？
examples.trans: Say, what do yakuza actually do during the daytime?

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: ねえ、ヤクザってさ、昼間何してんの？
examples.trans: Say, what do yakuza actually do during the daytime?

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

なら.gloss: if it is; in the case of

meanings.note: Conditional topic marker placed right after a noun or pronoun (あなたなら 'if it were you').

examples.text: あなたならどうしますか？
examples.trans: If it were you, what would you do?

examples.text: 明日なら時間があります。
examples.trans: If it is tomorrow, I have time.

examples.text: そんなことしたら世の中がめちゃくちゃになりますよ！
examples.trans: If you aired things like that on television, society would fall apart!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Marks the presence of a person (責任者はいるか) or follows て-form (often contracted to てる/てます in speech).

examples.text: バイトみたいに言うなよ。そんな簡単に辞めらんねえんだよ。
examples.trans: Don't talk like it is a part-time job. You can't quit that easily.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Auxiliary na-adjective expressing resemblance or conjecture.

examples.trans: It looks like it's going to rain.

examples.text: 彼は忙しいみたいですね。

そんな.gloss: such; that kind of; that much

meanings.note: Before たくさん, means 'that huge an amount'.

examples.text: そんな話は知りません。
examples.trans: I do not know such a story.

examples.text: そんな高いものは買えません。
examples.trans: I cannot buy something that expensive.

meanings.en: turn toward; face; be suited for
meanings.note: Godan verb; in 気が向く, means 'to feel like doing'.

examples.text: 気が向いたら連絡してください。
examples.trans: Please contact me whenever you feel like it.

examples.text: こっちを向いてください。

meanings.en: open a store; bring out; hand in
meanings.note: 店を出す means opening a branch; 出しやがって attaches tough-guy disdainful やがる.

examples.text: 駅前に新しい店を出します。
examples.trans: We open a new branch in front of the station.

examples.text: 書類を出してください。

meanings.en: do a favor for the speaker
meanings.note: After a te-form (会ってくれる？), warmly asks 'will you do that for us?'

examples.trans: Will you come again for me?

examples.text: 母が料理を作ってくれました。
examples.trans: My mother cooked food for me.

meanings.note: Prefixed to native Japanese words (お店, お二人, お持ち帰り) to add politeness.
Subsidiary ichidan verb written in hiragana after て-form (～てみる).

examples.text: 一度食べてみてください。
やってみなければ分かりません。
examples.trans: You won't know unless you try.

meanings.en: go home; leave and go back
meanings.note: Repeated past form 帰った、帰った! is an idiomatic shooing command ('off you go, go on home!').

examples.text: 帰る方向一緒だしよ、また送ってやるよ。
examples.trans: It is on my way back anyway, so I will walk you home again.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Used in everyday farewells like またね, また明日, and また会いましょう.

examples.text: また明日会いましょう。

meanings.note: Checks agreement ('isn't it?') or softens a request or farewell.
